skill.name: cloud-penetration-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized cloud security assessments across AWS, Azure, and GCP, including reconnaissance, IAM review, resource enumeration, misconfiguration validation, and reporting.
skill.summary: Plan and document authorized multi-cloud security assessments with clear scope and remediation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms substantial offensive cloud security content, including metadata credential retrieval, secret extraction, password spraying, persistence, and data exfiltration workflows. Some static findings are scanner noise from Markdown backticks, code fences, user-agent versions, and defensive encryption checks. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Credential harvesting and secret extraction procedures are presented as actionable steps.
remediation.suggestion: Remove direct secret-dumping, credential-store copying, and compromised-key examples, or replace them with read-only validation and sanitized reporting guidance.

remediation.issue: Persistence and backdoor creation workflows are included for Azure and AWS.
remediation.suggestion: Delete instructions for creating backdoor service principals, admin users, privileged role assignments, and new access keys.

remediation.issue: Password spraying and IP rotation examples can enable credential attacks.
remediation.suggestion: Replace password spraying procedures with policy review, lockout-safe simulation, and approved identity-provider audit methods.

remediation.issue: Metadata service token retrieval is documented as an exploitation step.
remediation.suggestion: Reframe metadata checks as defensive hardening validation, and avoid commands that retrieve tokens or credential paths.

remediation.issue: Installer guidance includes direct remote script execution and elevated installer execution.
remediation.suggestion: Use provider documentation, checksums, package managers, and explicit user confirmation instead of pipe-to-shell or unverified privileged installs.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Harvesting And Secret Extraction Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill teaches multiple ways to locate or extract secrets, including password-like user attributes, Key Vault secret values, Lambda environment variables, EC2 user data, and GCP credential stores.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections explicitly search for passwords, show cloud secrets, write environment variables and user data, and copy GCP credential configuration. These are direct credential-harvesting workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Persistence Backdoor Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill provides steps to create privileged service principals, add them to Global Admin, create new admin users, and create AWS access keys for persistence.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited headings and commands explicitly describe backdoor service principals, backdoor access keys, admin-user creation, and privileged role assignment. This is persistent cloud compromise guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Password Spraying And IP Rotation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes Azure password spraying and FireProx IP rotation examples, plus logic that records valid credentials during spraying.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples use MSOLSpray, FireProx, password lists, and valid-creds output. The intent is credential attack automation, not only defensive validation.

semantic_findings.title: Cloud Data Exfiltration Examples
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows copying cloud storage data to local paths and writing sensitive cloud inventory outputs to local files for later review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections include storage sync commands to local directories, an example local loot directory, and writing Lambda environment variables and EC2 user data to files. This supports data collection beyond simple inventory.

semantic_findings.title: Stealth And Detection Avoidance Advice
semantic_findings.description: The skill advises slow enumeration, delays, regional spreading, and multiple credentials to avoid triggering cloud monitoring during testing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited detection and troubleshooting sections discuss alerts, slow enumeration, delays, spreading across regions, and multiple credentials. Those details can help evade detection during misuse.

content.user_title: Assess Cloud Security Across AWS, Azure, and GCP
content.value_statement: Cloud security teams need repeatable assessment workflows across different providers. This skill organizes authorized multi-cloud testing, evidence capture, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Structures assessment phases for Azure, AWS, and GCP environments.
Lists common commands for cloud authentication, enumeration, and resource inventory.
Highlights IAM, storage, compute, serverless, and metadata service review areas.
References tools such as ScoutSuite, Pacu, AzureHound, ROADTools, and cloud_enum.
Supports report planning with findings, risk ratings, credential observations, and remediation notes.
limitations: Requires explicit written authorization and a defined scope before any testing.
Includes offensive examples that are unsafe for unsupervised or automated execution.
Does not replace provider documentation, legal review, or production change controls.
May require cloud credentials, tenant access, and provider-specific tooling not included in the skill.

use_cases.title: Plan A Scoped Cloud Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a provider-aware test plan that separates discovery, identity review, resource inventory, and reporting tasks.

use_cases.title: Review Multi-Cloud IAM Exposure
use_cases.description: Map users, roles, service principals, groups, and policies across AWS, Azure, and GCP for authorized review.

use_cases.title: Prepare Remediation Evidence
use_cases.description: Turn assessment observations into clear findings, affected resources, risk explanations, and hardening actions.

prompt_templates.title: Define The Assessment Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized cloud security assessment plan for AWS, Azure, and GCP. Include scope assumptions, required approvals, evidence to collect, and reporting sections.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Resource Inventory Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a checklist for enumerating cloud resources in a scoped assessment. Cover identity, compute, storage, databases, serverless, networking, and logging.

prompt_templates.title: Assess IAM And Secret Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe IAM and secret exposure review for an authorized cloud tenant. Include evidence fields, risk criteria, and remediation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Multi-Cloud Findings Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a professional findings report from authorized cloud assessment notes. Include executive summary, affected assets, impact, evidence summary, and prioritized remediation.

output_examples.input: A security consultant asks for a first-pass cloud assessment plan.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering authorization, asset discovery, IAM review, storage exposure checks, compute review, evidence handling, and report delivery.

output_examples.input: A platform team provides notes about exposed storage and broad IAM permissions.
output_examples.output: A prioritized findings outline with affected services, business impact, likely causes, and specific hardening recommendations.

output_examples.input: An auditor needs a defensible checklist for AWS, Azure, and GCP.
output_examples.output: A provider-specific checklist that separates identity, network, compute, storage, database, serverless, and logging controls.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target accounts, time windows, and data-handling rules before using the skill.
Prefer read-only validation and evidence collection unless the rules of engagement permit active testing.
Record commands, timestamps, affected assets, and remediation decisions for each confirmed finding.
anti_patterns: Do not run credential extraction, persistence, or password spraying steps outside an approved engagement.
Do not copy cloud credential stores or service account keys unless the rules of engagement explicitly allow it.
Do not use production customer data as proof when configuration metadata is enough.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for automatic agent execution?
faq.answer: No. It contains offensive cloud testing commands and should require human review, authorization, and scope confirmation.

faq.question: Which cloud providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and some Microsoft 365 security assessment workflows.

faq.question: Does it include reporting guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes assessment reports, resource inventories, credential findings, and remediation recommendations.

faq.question: Can it replace a legal rules-of-engagement document?
faq.answer: No. The skill assumes written authorization, defined scope, approved methods, and clear data-handling requirements.

faq.question: Can it be used for defensive cloud hardening?
faq.answer: Yes, when limited to authorized inventory, configuration review, evidence collection, and remediation planning.

faq.question: What is the main operational risk?
faq.answer: The main risk is that offensive examples could be misused to collect credentials, create persistence, or access cloud metadata.
